newsitem.title: FRANCE: BMW says Austria also candidate for engine plant.
newsitem.headline: BMW says Austria also candidate for engine plant.

text.p: The chairman of Bayerischen Motoren Werke (BMW) said on Tuesday that he was in favour of Britain becoming the location for a new engine plant but he said Austria was still in the running.

Bernd Pischetsrieder told a news conference during the Paris car show, called to announce a joint-venture deal in Latin America with Chrysler Corp, that he had told Trade and Industry secretary Ian Lang that he would like Britain to win the plant, but it still depended on subsidies.
"I favour making this engine in the UK provided we get the subsidies," he told reporters.
The other location in the running is Steyer in Austria.

The plant, which would create thousands of jobs in the Midlands region of Britain, would turn out 450,000 1.8 and 2.0 litre engines per year at full capacity. BMW is expected to decide in the next few weeks whether to build the plant.
BMW would build the engine in Britain alone, he said, adding that it would not involve Chrysler.
